questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code coordinates its locking with the carrier worker threads when producing a quote? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two threads call quote() for two different lanes at the same time, with no cached quotes. How do their carrier lookups proceed?
choices: Both lanes are fetched in parallel, since the cache is keyed by lane.
The lookups are interleaved on the 4-thread pool, with each future.get() waiting for its own tasks.
The calls are serialized: the second waits for the first to finish all its carrier calls, whatever the lane.
The second call fails fast because the monitor is already held.

questions.prompt: One carrier's basePrice() throws a RuntimeException while the other carriers answer normally. What does the caller of quote() observe?
choices: The best price among the carriers that succeeded is returned and cached.
An ExecutionException wrapping the failure is thrown, and nothing is cached for the lane.
A null quote is returned and cached for the lane.
The exception is thrown immediately and the remaining carrier tasks are cancelled.

questions.prompt: fuelIndex and fuelIndexFetchedAt are volatile, and currentFuelIndex() reads fuelIndexFetchedAt without holding any lock. What does volatile give that unsynchronized read?
choices: Mutual exclusion between pool threads and the thread that refreshes the index.
It guarantees that only one thread ever refreshes the index per hour.
Atomic updates of the pair so a reader never sees a new index with an old timestamp.
Pool threads see the values written by the refreshing thread promptly, without being told to wait for a monitor.
